name: Expo Skills
what: Official agent skills from the Expo team that teach coding agents how to build, upgrade and ship Expo and React Native apps: Expo Router, native UI and animation, data fetching, SDK upgrades, native modules, and the EAS services for builds, updates, hosting, workflows and store submission. Framework skills cover free Expo features; service skills cover EAS, which has paid plans. The Claude Code and Codex plugins also register Expo's hosted MCP server. MIT licensed.
who: Developers building Expo or React Native apps with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor or another skills-capable agent who want it to follow current Expo practice instead of older patterns.

setup.text: Any agent that supports skills: run this in your project root, then restart the agent. Add --agent <agent> to target a specific one:
Claude Code (plugin from the official marketplace):
Keep them current with npx skills@latest update (or name one skill, such as expo-router). Experimental skills are in a separate expo-experiments plugin.

The plugin's MCP server is Expo's remote server at https://mcp.expo.dev/mcp. It needs an Expo account and signs in with OAuth (run /mcp in Claude Code or codex mcp login expo). Expo's docs mark some tools, such as documentation search, as needing a paid EAS plan.

prompts: Add a settings screen with a native tab bar using Expo Router.
Upgrade this project to the latest Expo SDK and fix anything that breaks.
Set up an EAS workflow that builds and submits the iOS app when I push to main.

seo.title: Expo Skills: official Expo agent skills for Claude Code, Codex and Cursor
seo.description: What Expo's official agent skills cover (Expo Router, SDK upgrades, EAS), how to install them with npx skills add or as a Claude Code or Codex plugin, and what needs a paid plan.

sections.heading: Framework skills and service skills
paragraphs: The repository splits skills into two groups. Framework skills (for example expo-router, expo-native-ui, expo-animation, expo-data-fetching and expo-upgrade) are about building the app and use free Expo tooling. Service skills (for example eas-workflows, eas-update, eas-hosting and eas-app-stores) drive EAS, Expo's hosted service, which has free and paid tiers.

sections.heading: How it relates to the Expo MCP server
paragraphs: The skills are instructions; the MCP server is a set of live tools (docs lookup, library install, EAS builds and workflows, simulator screenshots with the expo-mcp package). The plugins bundle both, but with npx skills add you get the skills only and can add the MCP server separately.

faq.q: Do I need an Expo account?
faq.a: Not for the skills themselves. The Expo MCP server and the EAS service skills need an Expo account, and some features need a paid EAS plan.

faq.q: Does it work with bare React Native?
faq.a: The skills are written for Expo projects. Some advice applies to React Native in general, but commands like npx expo install and EAS assume Expo.
